Activate sustained formalization of Route 04. Start with the weighted finite-cover estimate and continue toward identifying which spinor transmission and differentiated-defect bounds control the residual curvature. Read and execute the launch prompt in:

/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md
I’ll read the Route 04 launch prompt, check the manuscript conventions and Lean environment, then formalize the weighted cover estimate and follow its hypotheses back to the collar analysis.

Route 02 already has a checked accounting theorem that accepts a different finite cover at each sequence index and truncation. I’ll connect Route 04 to that theorem and check the step before integration: why the self-dual projection removes the Clifford trace and leaves precisely the \(W^+\) term.

The weighted cover estimate now compiles, including overlaps, empty covers and a separate floor on each strip. Lean also verifies the factor \(1/2\) in the projected curvature identity for a compatible spin two-jet. I’m connecting that calculation to actual coordinate derivatives and checking when first-order transmission supplies enough information to bound the residual.

Lean now proves the Ricci forcing identity for the differentiated harmonic equation. On a protected annulus, this identifies the extra input beyond incoming trace control: a bound on \(\||\mathrm{Ric}|\,|\psi|\|_{L^2}\) in the larger buffer, together with control of normalization on the inner region. I’ve also checked an alternative using relative spinor gradients that avoids a uniform floor.

The weighted cover and curvature identities passed their individual Lean checks. The checkout disconnected during final integration. I’ll check which build results were recorded so I can report precisely what was verified.

The checkout is back. Lean has now verified the full normal-chart calculation, including the Levi–Civita connection term, and the cutoff derivative used when the joint spinor mass has no uniform lower bound. I’m running the public-import and blueprint checks on the combined result.

Route 04 now gives Route 02 a **Lean-verified criterion for vanishing residual chiral curvature**. On a finite cover of the physical remainder \(R\), let \(S_j=\sum_a|\psi_{ja}|^2\) be the joint spinor mass and \(H_j=\sum_a|\Pi(d^\nabla P\psi_{ja})^+|^2\) the squared projected twistor derivative. The normal-frame calculation gives \(2H_j=|W^+|^2S_j\). If \(S_j\ge c_j^2>0\) on each strip, then
\[
E_+(R)\le E_+\!\left(R\setminus\bigcup_j U_j\right)
+\sum_j\frac{2}{c_j^2}\int_{R\cap U_j}H_j.
\]
Each strip may use its own conformal gauge once its restricted energy measure is matched to the physical one. The strips may overlap, and the uncovered energy enters once.

**Transmission supplies only part of the curvature estimate.** On the homogeneous round cylinder, the squared midpoint mass is bounded by \(e^{-3L/2}\) times the squared incoming mass. Thus bounded incoming data cannot sustain a fixed positive midpoint floor as the collar length grows. On a protected annulus with a floor \(c\), the differentiated estimate also requires the Ricci forcing \(\||\mathrm{Ric}|\,|\psi|\|_{L^2}\) on a larger annulus, together with the local elliptic comparison and incoming mismatch bounds. [Derivation and transmission estimates](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/reviews/TRANSMISSION_AND_RESIDUAL_20261125.md)

There is also a criterion **without a uniform floor**. Under the local regularized Bochner inequality, bounded summed curvature-square cost and vanishing Ricci-square, relative-gradient fourth-power, cutoff, and uncovered costs imply the Route 02 energy identity. The next geometric step is to prove that local inequality for the covector-twisted operator and establish the summed bounds on an actual approximately critical sequence. [Dated continuation](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/continuation-notes/AFTER_WEIGHTED_COVER_20261125.md)

The full package and both blueprint formats built. All 192 public checks across 26 new modules passed with only standard Lean axioms. Chat capture remained unavailable because the exact thread source could not be retrieved. [Verification record](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/research-progress/handoffs/INTEGRATION_20261125.md)

Resume sustained Route 04 in the smooth-poincare-4d checkout with the author's selected lead and bounded gpt-6.2-sol/ultra helpers. Read AGENTS.md, the formalization workflow, Route 04 register, TRANSMISSION_AND_RESIDUAL_20261125.md, the integration return and this note. Recompute the working manuscript/Lean revisions. Reuse the publicly checked normal-coordinate twistor and Ricci contractions, variable-cover constructors and signed analytic estimates. Begin with the compactly supported covector-twisted Bochner/Dirac square and its integrated regularized inequality on the actual annular metric; this is still a hypothesis of spinRelativeBochner_bound. In parallel work toward the L²-forcing, H¹-domain incoming inverse in the fixed unit-round spectral model. Keep local bundle identifications, pole and normalization, both endpoints, inner and outer measures, finite norms, and joint zero or uncovered energy explicit. Try the relative-gradient criterion when no uniform floor survives. Compare new source revisions and actual receipts; do not claim coverage or smooth recognition from either identified interface alone. Accept through the public import with lake build, #check and #print axioms, blueprint and register updates, and continue through useful ready dependencies.

I’ll recheck the Route 04 handoff and current sources, then pursue the annular Bochner estimate and the two-ended spectral inverse in parallel. I’ll track which geometric hypotheses each proof still needs.

The pointwise square now compiles with the cotangent curvature acting by the negative transpose. Lean also verifies the sharp bound \(\lvert W^+\rvert^2\sum_a|\psi_a|^2\leq4\sum_a|\nabla^2\psi_a|^2\) for compatible harmonic jets. I’m connecting these pointwise results to integration in the annular metric.

The spectral inverse now handles arbitrary square-integrable forcing and reconstructs one absolutely continuous Hilbert-valued field with both endpoint traces. On the geometric side, the physical-volume estimate now follows from compactly supported Green identities and first-order chart data. I’m checking the joint-zero case and the identification of the two chiral fibers before the final package audit.

A flat harmonic spinor gives an exact test of the no-floor criterion. Its only zero has measure zero, yet its relative fourth-power cost on \(a<|x|\le b\) is \(32\pi^2\log(b/a)\). I’m checking how a second harmonic spinor changes that cost and which metric identifications the annular proof can derive from the moving frame.

Route 04 now derives the regularized curvature estimate in the **actual annular metric volume** from the covector-twisted Dirac square and compactly supported Green identity. The proof gives coefficient \(816\) once the local spin fields, cutoff tests and their first derivatives are identified in the metric gauge. The integrated inequality was previously a hypothesis. [Derivation and hypotheses](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/notes/ANNULAR_BOCHNER_AND_WEAK_INVERSE_20261125.md)

The no-floor calculation identifies a precise obstruction. A flat harmonic spinor with a single zero has \(S=|\psi|^2=r^2\) and \(Q=|\nabla\psi|^2=4\), so
\[
\int_{a<|x|\le b}(Q/S)^2\,dx=32\pi^2\log(b/a).
\]
Adding a nonzero parallel spinor makes the cost finite on every bounded ball, but that cost diverges as the companion’s amplitude tends to zero. Thus even a family with no common zero at any sequence index can lose uniform control. [Two-field proof](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/FirstOrderTwistor/SpinComplementaryFamily.lean)

The **fixed spectral cylinder** now has an incoming inverse for arbitrary \(L^2\) forcing and half-order incoming data. Positive modes take data at \(0\), negative modes at \(L\), and one absolutely continuous Hilbert-valued field realizes both endpoint traces. Transfer to a geometric collar still requires its spin eigenbasis, Sobolev norms, and pole-normalized boundary data.

For residual curvature, the remaining step is to bound the **summed** Ricci, relative-gradient and cutoff costs on one physical sequence and account for the Weyl energy on joint-zero or uncovered regions. Coverage and smooth recognition remain open. [Continuation](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/04_dirac_collar_transmission/continuation-notes/AFTER_ANNULAR_BOCHNER_AND_WEAK_INVERSE_20261125.md)

`lake build` passed. All **226 new public declaration and axiom checks** passed across 27 modules using only standard Lean axioms. The blueprint and register were updated.
